name: Statistical Reversion
rationale: Statistical reversion rules test whether price deviations from a recent distribution revert enough to beat costs.
expected_benefit: Potential short-horizon risk-adjusted return improvement with lower average exposure.
failure_modes: Persistent trends can crush reversion entries.
Distribution assumptions can break during crises.
required_project_capabilities: rolling mean and standard deviation indicators

canonical_variants.name: Bollinger Band reversion
canonical_variants.description: Enter after price closes below a lower band and exit after mean recovery.
canonical_variants.hypothesis_template: A Bollinger Band pullback rule may improve Sharpe by buying statistically stretched declines.
canonical_variants.minimum_acceptable_performance: Improve Sharpe and retain at least 60% of benchmark CAGR after realistic costs.

canonical_variants.name: Moving-average distance reversion
canonical_variants.description: Enter when price is far below a moving average and exit near the average.
canonical_variants.hypothesis_template: A moving-average distance reversion rule may improve returns by buying unusually deep pullbacks.
canonical_variants.minimum_acceptable_performance: Improve Sharpe with no worse max drawdown than buy-and-hold.

canonical_variants.name: Rolling-low reversion
canonical_variants.description: Enter near a rolling low and exit after a simple recovery condition.
canonical_variants.hypothesis_template: A rolling-low reversion rule may identify short-term capitulation without needing standard-deviation bands.
canonical_variants.minimum_acceptable_performance: Improve Sharpe versus buy-and-hold after realistic costs.

suggested_validation: Use one entry threshold and one exit rule first.
Run cost sensitivity because average edge may be small.
Separate crisis periods from normal pullback periods.
execution_notes: Rolling-low variants are executable. Bollinger/z-score variants need rolling standard deviation or arithmetic expression support.
